unit.name: Around the World in 80 Days × Atlanta

situation.text: Hoje você conhece Bethany, de Atlanta. Países e nacionalidades.

pages.goal: Hoje você aprende a dizer de onde você é com I’m from + país ou cidade, como um viajante que dá a volta ao mundo.

pages.hook: In the USA, “Where are you from?” is a very common way to start a chat. People are curious and often want to talk about food, music and travel.

mythfact.s: Atlanta is the capital of the state of Georgia.
mythfact.why: Atlanta is the capital and the biggest city of Georgia.
It was invented there in 1886 and the company is still based in Atlanta.

mythfact.s: “American” means “from the USA” in everyday English.
mythfact.why: People say “I’m American” for a person from the United States.

mythfact.s: In the USA, everybody only speaks English.
mythfact.why: Spanish and many other languages are spoken in homes across the country.

decode.q: Which languages can you use at this shop?
decode.why: The sign lists English, Español (Spanish) and Français (French).

compare.br: In Brazil, people often ask “De onde você é?” and then talk about the state or the city, like São Paulo or Bahia.
compare.us: In the USA, people can answer with a city, a state or a country. Many families have roots in other countries too.
compare.tip: Say your city first, then your country: “I’m from São Paulo, in Brazil.”
compare.ask: Say where you are from and which languages you speak.

quiz.q: To say your country, you say…
“Do you speak Portuguese?” — a short answer is…

pages.polite: Be curious and kind. After “Where are you from?” add “Nice!” or “I love…” and keep the chat warm.

pages.title: Reading quest — Many countries, one hallway
text: My name is Aisha, and I live in Atlanta, Georgia. Last month a new neighbor moved to my building. She said, “Hi! I’m from **Brazil**. **Where are you from?**” I answered, “**I’m from Atlanta**.”

She told me, “**I speak Portuguese and English**.” I said, “**I speak English and a little French**.” We laughed because our hallway now has four languages: English, Portuguese, French and Spanish. My other neighbor is from Mexico.

I love Brazilian food, so I asked, “**Where is your family from?**” She said, “**They’re from São Paulo**.” It is a very big **city**. Atlanta is big too, and many people live here. Coca-Cola started in my city in 1886.

This reminds me of a famous book. In 1872, the French writer Jules Verne wrote “Around the World in 80 Days”. An Englishman, Phileas Fogg, makes a bet. He goes **around the world** by train and by boat. He visits many **countries** and meets many people. At each new place, he is a stranger.

My neighbor is a little like Mr. Fogg. She is far from home, but she is not afraid. “**Nice to meet you**,” I told her, “and **welcome**!” She smiled. In my building, the world is only one floor away.
